subject: Future Tech
title: Decoding Brain Signals
description: A quick, practical guide to Decoding Brain Signals.

hook.text: Decoding means translating raw neural activity into something meaningful, like a word, a movement, or a choice.

buildup.text: Researchers record brain signals while a person performs known tasks. The data trains a decoder to spot patterns.

discovery.text: Deep learning made decoding far more accurate. Neural networks find subtle patterns humans would never notice.

twist.text: Decoders still fail on novel thoughts. They work best when the set of possible outputs is small and well-defined.

climax.text: Today's best decoders can reconstruct imagined handwriting at 90 characters per minute from brain activity alone.

punchline.text: The brain writes in code. Decoders are learning to read it.

quiz.question: What technology dramatically improved brain signal decoding accuracy?
